statement: The language Bipartite is the set of bipartite graphs. Local proofs of constant size exist for this language: the prover can just describe a 2-coloring of the graph by giving a bit to each node, and every node can check that its neighbors are given a color different from its own. We conjecture that for this language, even when restricting the topology to cycles, optimal purely global proofs are larger than the sum of the optimal local proof sizes. More precisely this sum is Θ(n), and we conjecture that purely global proofs take Θ(n log n) bits.
